verdict.reasoning: Patient reports onset 2–3 days ago and exertional symptoms: "about two to three days ago, I was running with a friend... I found myself actually short of breath... definitely... if I'm walking briskly now."

Patient uses blue inhaler daily PRN with poor effect: "I'm having... short of breath... and I've used my blue inhaler but to no avail" and later "yeah, and morning or evening to kinda prevent it as well" and "I'm just using that as and when I have symptoms."

Patient confirms preventer (brown) inhaler is used twice daily: Doctor: "How are you using the ? Is it twice a day?" Patient: "Um, yes" and later doctor refers to "the brown your Clenil. The brown inhaler."
Baseline peak flow approximated as 380: Doctor: "So, what was what's your peak flow reading when you're good?... Let's see it's about, um, three eighty, yeah?" Patient agrees: "Yeah."

Timing and lack of steroids/admissions are confirmed: "When was the last time you had an asthma attack?" Patient: "about three to four years ago." Then, "have you ever been admitted in hospital because your was so bad?" Patient: "no" and "have you ever had oral steroids in the past?" Patient: "no."
Last asthma review: Doctor: "When was the last time you had an asthma review with our nurse?" Patient: "about two years ago." Doctor repeats "Two years ago."
Hay fever and no drug allergies documented: Patient: "I have hay fever." Doctor: "Now any allergies to medication?" Patient: "Ohh no" and doctor concludes "So you're not allergic to anything?"
PRN Salbutamol use: Patient: "I'm Salbutamol... that I'm taking as well" and later "I think I'm using that every day and the Salbutamol just like as and when."
Clenil as preventer twice daily: Doctor identifies "the brown your Clenil. The brown inhaler" and earlier confirms usage: "How are you using the ? Is it twice a day?" Patient: "Um, yes."
Cetraben use: Patient initially lists "Salbutamol, Flanel Bactroban and Hydrocortisone" then corrects: "Er, Cetraben and Hydrocortisone." indicating current Cetraben use.
Topical hydrocortisone use: Patient: "Er, Cetraben and Hydrocortisone." Context is skin treatment linked to suspected eczema, consistent with topical hydrocortisone.

Doctor describes a small exacerbation and patient reports 2–3 days of SOB and wheeze: Doctor: "it looks like you can be having a small, small exacerbation" and patient: "I'm just wheezing a bit, and coughing and just generally a bit short of breath" beginning "about two to three days ago" during exertion.
Allergic history: Patient states "I have hay fever."

Dose increase for Clenil: Doctor: "the brown your Clenil... If you're using just three puffs twice a day, you can increase it to four puffs twice a day." and reiterates "increase your brown inhaler to four puffs twice a day."

Salbutamol usage and A&E advice: Doctor: "you can use your blue inhaler as and when... maximum about every two to four... hours" and "if you're using it that often... your asthma is really bad" and "if your breathing is getting really worse, then you would need to take yourself to A and E."

Follow-up plan: Doctor: "I would like you to be seen by one of our GP's in the next few days" and later "we're gonna examine your chest... Make you do the peak flow reading" and "book an appointment to see and I will recommend that meet her face to face."
